write_up: You’ve moved from tutoring at City Year Baltimore to managing a youth workforce program at Harbor Pathways. A recruiter could move this forward for a Program Manager, Youth Workforce role, with questions about how many students and employers the program reaches.

Your summer jobs line is the best model: it names the program, the students and where they’re placed. The promotion from coordinator to manager is easy to follow, and your team numbers show the responsibility you hold now.

Let’s start with the summer jobs line, then explain what your coordinators and seasonal staff do. Add the number of employer partners you recruit and onboard if you have it. Those details will give a recruiter a fuller picture of the program you manage.

cards.line: - Manage a summer jobs program placing high school students with local employers
cards.cannot_tell: This names the work well, but a recruiter can't tell how many students the program places. That's a useful measure for a youth workforce role.
cards.example: Manage a summer jobs program placing [number] high school students with local employers per [time period]
cards.question: How many high school students does the program place, and over what period?

cards.line: - Supervise 4 program coordinators and 20 seasonal staff
cards.cannot_tell: The team numbers are useful, but a recruiter can't tell what the coordinators and seasonal staff do under your supervision.
cards.example: Supervise 4 program coordinators and 20 seasonal staff who [team responsibilities]
cards.question: What do the coordinators and seasonal staff handle?

cards.question: How many employer partners do you recruit and onboard, over what period, and what do they participate in?

fit.note: Your experience points toward nonprofit youth workforce program management. Your progression at Harbor Pathways also shows experience coordinating student workshops and employer-facing work.
